records.name: Bazilijus
records.facts_used: Bazilijus is the Lithuanian form paired with Basilius in the Senn–Salys dictionary. The family goes back to Greek Basileios, “royal”, related to basileus, “king”. An early historical bearer is Basil the Great, called Bazilijus Didysis in Lithuanian: he became bishop of Caesarea in 370 and died on 1 January 379. These dates concern the ancient bearer; they do not date the arrival of this Lithuanian spelling.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.

records.name: Esme
records.facts_used: Rajandi places Esme among Estonian feminine names and compares its meaning with Prima, “first, firstborn”. This is a semantic comparison, not a statement that Esme was borrowed from Latin or that it is the French name Esmé. The form and its relationships are documented in Edgar Rajandi’s Raamat nimedest, published in Tallinn in 1966. The book records the naming traditions known at that time. Its publication date documents a linguistic treatment, rather than the name’s invention or its first birth registration.
